text:
customer_acme: hey, we've got a high-volume job where clients are aborting streams mid-response. Redwood shows a bunch of 5xx on our dashboard and we were billed for tokens after the client disconnected. can you check?
maya_support: sorry about that — can you paste a request_id or sample log? rough timeframe helps.
customer_acme: sure, the most recent: request_id=rid-2026-03-14-84f2, client logs show "write: broken pipe" then the UI shows the tokens consumed up to the end. our SDK aborts after 2s of inactivity.
evan_sre: tagging with :eyes: — is this coming from our edge proxy returning 502/504, or are we the one returning 5xx? can you attach the gateway edges_log for that request id?
customer_acme: i pasted a snippet: 
```
EDGE: 2026-03-14T18:02:11Z rid-2026-03-14-84f2 status=500 msg="upstream write: connection reset by peer" backend=gw1
CLIENT: abort() called after timeout, connection closed by client
```
maya_support: thanks. I forwarded logs to eng-sre. is this different from the "client disconnect counted as 5xx" threads from earlier? looks similar but our customer says billing was applied despite client abort.
evan_sre: initial read — edge sees upstream write error, then we currently map many upstream write/pipeclose errors to 5xx for surface-level SLOs and billing. if client closes before final chunk, gateway sometimes treats as server failure because it couldn't finish the response stream.
tara_billing: from billing POV we exclude obvious client 4xx aborts, but if the server returned a 5xx we bill. we need to determine whether the upstream error is caused by the client or by our runtime.
maya_support: customer can repro easily — they shared a small repro using Node fetch + AbortController. may I share it with you?
customer_acme: yep — here: 
```
const controller = new AbortController();
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses/stream', { method: 'POST', body: jsonPayload, signal: controller.signal })
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 2000)
```
When they abort, redwood logs the upstream write error and a 500 is recorded.
evan_sre: thanks. hypothesis: our gateway tries to finish streaming the last chunk to the client; if client half-closes at that moment we get `EPIPE`/`ECONNRESET` from the socket while still writing to client. our current metric path increments a 5xx counter and emits a 5xx to the caller. the underlying L7 proxy should probably translate that to a client-abort classification (499-ish) rather than a server error.
ops-bot: deploy queued: patch/proxy-classify-client-aborts-if-write-fails-499 (PR #4127) by evan_sre — testing bucket attached.
evan_sre: developing quick instrument: add heuristics — if we saw final upstream chunk successfully generated and then socket write failed within X ms of client FIN, mark as client_abort and don't bill/ping SLO. need to run this at the edge without impacting streaming perf.
tara_billing: if we change classification we must update billing ledger retroactively for any accounts in the affected window. ops, can we isolate affected request_ids in a 3-hour window starting 2026-03-14T17:30Z?
evan_sre: yes, I can run a query to find `upstream write` + `connection reset by peer` lines and correlate to billing logs. will post a list.
maya_support: customer — we'll run the repro against staging with the PR applied and confirm billing behavior. can you confirm the SDK version used?
customer_acme: using acme-sdk v2.1.1 in prod. staging uses the same pattern so should repro. thanks for the quick attention. :thumbsup:
evan_sre: interim mitigation: disable aggressive server retry on chunk flush and lower the server write buffer so we fail-fast and log a client_abort path. that'll reduce misclassified 5xx while we push the PR.
maya_support: recording action items: 1) evan run log query + list affected request_ids; 2) apply staging patch, run customer repro; 3) tara prepare billing remediations if we flip classification; 4) update docs/FAQ about streaming aborts and billing.
customer_acme: appreciate it. one more ask — can you confirm we won't be charged for these in prod until this is resolved?
tara_billing: we'll freeze billing for the request_ids we determine were client-abort misclassified once evan's list is ready. will follow up in this thread.
evan_sre: putting query here for reproducibility: 
```
SELECT rid FROM edge_logs WHERE message LIKE '%upstream write%' AND timestamp >= '2026-03-14T17:30:00Z' AND timestamp <= '2026-03-14T20:30:00Z';
```
will attach CSV soon.
maya_support: thanks all. i'll keep customer updated and mark this as a P1 support escalation until we confirm remediation.
ops-bot: incident-note: customer_acme streaming-misclass-escalation created (INC-2026-114).
